entry.title: 📧 How to Validate Email Addresses in PHP: A Practical Guide
entry.summary: Why Email Validation Matters Whether you’re building a contact form, newsletter signup, or user registration, validating email addresses is essential to: Avoid fake or malformed emails in your database. Improve deliverability of emails you send. Provide a better user experience by catching typos early. PHP makes email validation simple and reliable with built-in functions and filters. ✅ Ways to Validate Emails in PHP Method 1: Using filter_var() **<?php user@example.com"; if (filter_var($email, FILTER_VALIDATE_EMAIL)) { **Output: user@example.com Method 2: Using Regular Expressions **<?php user@example.com"; if (preg_match("/^[\w-.]+@([\w-]+.)+[\w-]{2,4}$/", $email)) { Bonus: Checking MX Records <?php user@example.com"; if (checkdnsrr($domain, "MX")) { 🧪 Best Practices for Email Validation Use filter_var() as your first step. Optionally, check MX records for domain validity. Avoid sending a real SMTP ping to check mailbox existence — it’s unreliable and can be seen as spammy. Always give users clear feedback if their email is invalid. 📌 Conclusion Make sure to implement email validation at both the client-side (JavaScript) and server-side (PHP) for the best results. UI/UX, you’ll improve your lead quality and user experience.

entry.title: Keyword,Return type,Method,Objects,Void&Variables...
entry.summary:
Keywords:
Static :
static keyword refers to class specific information.
Static keyword have only one memory copy.
In the static keyword class can common for all object.
Non-static:
Non-Static Keyword refers to object specific information.
Non static have multiple memory copy.
In the non static keyword object have the specific information.
Return Type:
The return statement is used to exit from a method and optionally pass a value back to the code that called the method.
Return statement is the last statement in the method definition.
If the method has a return type (like int, String, boolean, etc.), return sends a value of that type back.
If the method is declared as void, return; simply ends the method early (and doesn’t return any value).
Example:
String buy() { System.out.println("buy method"); return "thank you" }
A method in Java is a block of code that performs a specific task. It is used to define behavior or functionality that can be reused. String buy() { System.out.println("buy method"); }
In Java, an object is an instance of a class. It represents a real-world entity with state (data) and behavior (methods). ## Key concepts: Class: A blueprint or template. Object: A real thing created from the blueprint. Home Person = new Home();
Home - Home is the name of the class.
Person - Person is the name of the variable.
new Home - new Home is the keyword used to create new object from the class.
Void:
This method does not return anything. It is used when a method performs an action, but doesn’t give back a result. Local variable declared in side the function or block. Global variable declared outside the function.

entry.title: Providing shared file storage on Azure
entry.summary:
How to Provide shared file storage STEP 1 In the portal, search for and select** Storage accounts.** Select + Create.
For Resource group select Create new. Give your resource group a name and select **OK **to save your changes. Provide a Storage account name. Ensure the name meets the naming requirements. Set the Performance to Premium. Set the Premium account type to File shares. Set the Redundancy to Zone-redundant storage. Select Review and then Create the storage account. Wait for the resource to deploy. Select Go to resource.
STEP 2 In the storage account, in the Data storage section, select the File shares blade.
Select + File share and provide a*Name*. Review the other options, but take the defaults. Select Create
STEP 3 Select your file share. In the Operations section, select the Snapshots blade. Select + Add snapshot. The comment is optional. Select OK. Select your snapshot and verify your file directory and uploaded file are included.
STEP 3a Search for and select Virtual networks.
Select Create. Select your resource group. and give the virtual network a name. Take the defaults for other parameters, select Review + create, and then Create.
Wait for the resource to deploy. Select Go to resource.
In the Settings section, select the Subnets blade. Select the default subnet. In the Service endpoints section **choose **Microsoft.Storage in the Services drop-down. Do not make any other changes. Be sure to Save your changes.
STEP 4 Return to your files storage account.
In the Security + networking **section, select the **Networking blade.
Change the Public network access to Enabled from selected virtual networks and IP addresses.
In the Virtual networks section, select Add existing virtual network. Select your virtual network and subnet, select Add.
Be sure to Save your changes. Select the Storage browser and navigate to your file share.
Verify the message not authorized to perform this operation. You are not connecting from the virtual network.
